I would say broadly:

1. Maine is weird

2. Never count out Susan Collins

3. If the typical left-populist recruit for statewide office was, like Jackson, a state legislator who over-performs electorally I would have much friendlier sentiments toward this movement

On paper Jackson is *extremely* strong — a lot of people who’ve seen him up close have doubts about his skills as a talker but his actual electoral track-record in his (admittedly very idiosyncratic) state senate district is very good.

Famous last words if I’m wrong, but given the way the Maine caucuses are structured I think the superior organizational capacity of TROY JACKSON’s operation (labor unions + Platner org remnants) are going to lead to him winning at the convention in a huge landslide.
